description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of languages used in the OpenAssistant Conversations dataset, with English dominating at 31.4% and Spanish following at 5.7%. Russian accounts for 5.8%, while German, French, Chinese, Thai, Portuguese (Brazil), and Catalan collectively make up the remaining 10.1%, with individual shares ranging from 1.6% to 3.6%. The “Other” category, which includes languages not individually listed, represents 5.8% of the total. The chart uses varying shades of blue to distinguish between categories, with English and Spanish highlighted in darker tones, and smaller segments in lighter shades. Percentages are labeled directly on or near each slice, and the largest segments are visually emphasized through size and placement. No legend is present, but labels are positioned adjacent to their respective slices for clarity. The data suggests a strong prevalence of English, followed by Spanish and Russian, with a long tail of less frequently represented languages.
